props.gloss_en: Rav Yehuda: one sounds a tekia and sounds a terua from within the tekia
Rav Asi: one sounds a tekia and a terua in one breath
Rav Asi instituted [the practice] in Huzal according to his teaching
the baraita: a Festival falling on Shabbat eve -- one sounds a tekia and does not sound a terua
Rav Yehuda's reading: 'does not sound a terua' means not a terua by itself, but [one does sound it] from within the tekia
Rav Asi's reading: 'does not sound a terua' means not in two breaths, but [one does sound it] in one breath

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: תוקעין ולא מריעין -- מאי לאו לא מריעין כלל? the baraita seems to forbid any terua, against Rav Yehuda's terua from within the tekia

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, רב יהודה מתרץ לטעמיה: not a terua by itself, but from within the tekia (= p_ry_lo_meriin_bifnei_atzmah)

objections.gloss_en: the same מיתיבי: if 'no terua' means none at all, it contradicts Rav Asi's tekia-and-terua in one breath

answered_by.gloss_en: ורב אסי מתרץ לטעמיה: not in two breaths, but in one breath (= p_ra_lo_meriin_bishtei_neshimot)
